name: sheet-music-analysis
description: Harmonic analysis of sheet music, drawn on the engraved score.

capabilities: Analyse harmony in a MusicXML score or a PDF of printed music
Draw the analysis on the engraved page
defaultPrompt: Analyse the harmony of bars 1-8 of this score.
Show me the phrases and cadences in this piece.
How do the voices move in bars 5-8?

positive.description: Full analysis of an attached score
positive.prompt: Analyse the harmony of bars 1-8 of this.
positive.expected_behavior: A card shows the engraved bars 1-8 with Roman numerals, labelled chord-function brackets, boxed cadences and numbered circles, with PNG and PDF links, followed by a short commentary.
The same bars redrawn with chords and brackets only (view harmony).
Bars 9-16 annotated in a card, with a commentary.

positive.prompt: Show the phrase structure of bars 1-16.
positive.expected_behavior: Bars 1-16 with phrase brackets and cadences (view form).

positive.description: Voice leading view, same chat as the first case
positive.prompt: How do the voices move in bars 5-8?
positive.expected_behavior: Bars 5-8 redrawn showing voice leading only (view voice_leading): arrows for the resolutions that matter, with a short explanation.

positive.description: Reading an attached PDF of printed music
positive.prompt: Can you analyse the harmony of this piece?
positive.expected_behavior: After up to a few minutes, a card shows the engraved music read from the PDF, with bars that may be misread shaded; without waiting for the user, a second card shows the analysis drawn on the score, with the same bars still shaded, and the reply briefly mentions them.

positive.description: The Analyse this score button (new chat)
positive.prompt: Can you read this PDF with the app?
positive.expected_behavior: A card shows the engraved music read from the PDF, with a button, Analyse this score. If the reply stops after the reading, tapping the button posts the message "Please analyse this score now." for the user, and a second card shows the analysis drawn on the score.

positive.prompt: Can you analyse the harmony of this piece?
positive.expected_behavior: A card shows the music read from the two scanned pages, with bars that may be misread shaded; a second card shows the analysis drawn on that reading. The reply ends by offering to read the scan carefully.

positive.description: Asking for the careful reading, same chat as the scanned PDF
positive.prompt: Please read this scan carefully instead.
positive.expected_behavior: Nothing is read yet. The reply says that reading a scan carefully takes about 5 minutes a page, that it downloads and runs a small measuring script from Sheet Music Analysis in the chat, and asks whether to go ahead.

positive.description: The careful reading itself, same chat
positive.expected_behavior: Over about 4 to 10 minutes ChatGPT reads each of the two pages itself and hands its reading in; a card then shows the analysis drawn on that careful reading, and the reply says the page shows its careful reading.

negative.description: General music theory question with no score: answered from general knowledge, no tool call.
negative.prompt: What is a Neapolitan sixth chord?

negative.description: Audio instead of a score: the app needs MusicXML or a PDF of printed music, so no tool call; the reply explains that.
negative.prompt: Here's an MP3 of my piece, can you analyse it?

negative.description: Editing or rewriting music is outside the app, which only analyses: no tool call.
negative.prompt: Transpose this score to D major and send me the new file.

publication.release_notes:
The card that shows what was read from your PDF has a button, Analyse this score, for when the analysis has not started by itself.
A scanned PDF is analysed straight away. The slower, careful reading is offered afterwards; it takes about 5 minutes a page.
A file with no notes in it is answered with a plain message instead of an empty analysis.
After a reading and after a draft, the chat is told the next step, so fewer analyses stop halfway.
